objections.claim: D-025 Decision 3 is a RULE-GOVERNED restatement of D-001 MF-6, so saying that a file-08 register-content change co-occurs with a D-000 or product-authority act does not amend D-001.
objections.evidence: D-001 MF-6 says register-content changes are decisions and that each named change gets its own D-000-reviewed entry and commit. D-025 replaces that mandatory conjunction with an alternative: a D-000 or product-authority act. A product-authority act can supply the substantive Route C decision, but the measured D-001 bytes do not let it substitute for the separately reviewed register-content act. As written, form (i) can be read to authorize a product-packet decision followed by a file-08 amendment with no D-000 review, while D-025 Decision 5 simultaneously says D-001 is not amended. This is the exact silent-authority change MF-6 was adopted to prevent.
objections.proposedFix: Restore D-001's actual rule: any resulting file-08 content change co-occurs with its own D-000-reviewed entry and commit; a product-authority act supplies or records the substantive decision but is not an alternative to that register-change review. If direct user disposition is intended to override that safeguard, say so as an explicit D-001 successor rather than attributing it to MF-6.

objections.claim: Each Route B selector remains completely overturnable by C-D0xx alone, and reverting C-D026 returns DR-002 to D-001's default, even after the selected disposition is authored and recorded.
objections.evidence: D-031 step 4 expressly schedules a later disposition for each adopted selector, each as its own reviewed entry recorded by the owning V1 authority. Once such a dependent entry lands, reverting only C-D026, C-D027, C-D028, C-D029, or C-D030 does not remove or supersede that recorded disposition. D-026's promised return to the default is then factually false, and the other four 'C-D0xx only' procedures no longer reverse the selected outcome. D-002's adopted overturn text already states the correct corpus rule: a one-revert path exists only before dependent commits; afterward a successor must disposition or supersede dependents. D-000 clauses 4 and 5 require decision-granular, genuinely cheaper reversal, not a commit label that leaves the operative downstream act standing.
objections.proposedFix: For every selector, state the temporal boundary: before any dependent disposition lands, supersession plus revert of C-D0xx is sufficient; after one lands, overturn also requires an owning-authority supersession or revert of each dependent disposition entry. Require every future disposition to name this dependency and its own rollback. Do not claim that the selector commit alone returns the row to its default after dependent acts exist.
